To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rich communication is a necessary condition for development, whereas asynchronous communication is necessary for learning.
asynchronous communication has a direct positive effect on learning competency, whereas rich communication has no direct effect.
asynchronous communication is a necessary condition for learning competency, whereas rich communication is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for development competency and NSD performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that communication modes play in the development of NSD competencies and their impact on NSD performance.
the interplay of communication modes and NSD competencies, and how this interplay affects the NSD performance link.
the nature of communication and the role of communication modes in the development of NSD competencies and NSD performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiplicative effect of communication modes is more important than their contingent effects for NSD competency development.
the multiplicative approach is the most appropriate one to use for understanding NSD performance.
the multiplicative nature of dual coding theory is more relevant to the NSD performance relationship than the contingent nature of media synchronicity and richness theories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asynchronous communication has a positive effect on learning competency, which in turn has a positive effect, mediated by development competency, on NSD performance.
the contingent approach is not sufficient for explaining the effects of communication on NSD.
rich communication and asynchronous communication have different effects on NSD performance, and that the effects of communication modes on competencies and NSD performance are conditional.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rich and asynchronous communication are not substitutes but complementary.
rich communication should be complemented with asynchronous communication to enhance the development competency and the performance of new service development.
the multiplicative approach to communication theory is a more appropriate lens for understanding NSD performance.
